# The typed no-region error names AWS_REGION as a fix, and it is not one — MEASURED

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` raises a typed `LLMConfigError` when no AWS region resolves, and its
message instructs the operator to set "a standard AWS region source (AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION /
the active profile's config)". The surrounding docstring says the same. **`AWS_REGION` alone does not
work**, so an operator who follows the error message exactly gets the identical error again, with
nothing to indicate why.

MEASURED in the production review-bot container (compose-review-bot-1 on i-00880b2c7f13527c5), on
**botocore 1.43.62 / boto3 1.43.62** — a NEWER version than the 1.43.58 the original finding was made
against, so this is not a stale observation:

    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION genuinely UNSET (env -u), AWS_REGION=us-east-1
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name is None
    both genuinely UNSET
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name is None
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1, AWS_REGION empty
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name == 'us-east-1'

So only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` (or a profile) resolves. This is exactly why
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets BOTH `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` for
the review-bot, and its inline comment already records the asymmetry correctly — the compose file is
right and the module docstring/error message are wrong, so the two disagree in-tree.

The blast radius is operator time during an outage, on a path that is fail-closed by design: the
Bedrock provider refuses to construct without a region, so this message is precisely what a
first-responder reads while the LLM-Review gate is not voting. Discovered while verifying the region
story for the production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a].

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — the `LLMConfigError` message and the module/function docstring
  that both list `AWS_REGION` as a working source.

Nothing else: no behaviour change, no config change. The pre-check that produces the error is correct
as written — it tests boto3's own resolution rather than inventing a default — and must not be altered.

## Approach

Correct the text to name `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` (and rebar's own `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`) as the
sources that resolve, and state explicitly that `AWS_REGION` alone does NOT, with the botocore version
the claim was measured against so a future reader can tell whether to re-measure rather than assuming.
Do not silently delete the `AWS_REGION` mention: an operator who has already set it needs to be told it
is insufficient, which a bare omission does not do.

## Testing

A test asserting the error message does not offer `AWS_REGION` as a standalone remedy would be a
change-detector on prose. The oracle worth having instead is the behavioural one this ticket rests on:
assert that with only `AWS_REGION` set, region resolution yields nothing and the typed
`LLMConfigError` is still raised — so if a future botocore makes `AWS_REGION` work, the test goes GREEN
in a way that flags the docstring as re-checkable rather than leaving it quietly wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the `LLMConfigError` message no longer presents `AWS_REGION` as a sufficient fix, and names
      `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` / `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as the sources that do resolve.
- [ ] the message or docstring states that `AWS_REGION` alone does not resolve, naming the botocore
      version the behaviour was measured on, so the claim is falsifiable rather than folklore.
- [ ] the module docstring and the error message agree with each other AND with the existing
      `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` review-bot comment, which already states the asymmetry
      correctly — the in-tree contradiction is gone.
- [ ] a test pins the BEHAVIOUR (only-`AWS_REGION` still fails to resolve and still raises the typed
      error), not the prose, and is verified RED by mutating the pre-check away.
compiled_state.title: bedrock_model.py tells operators to set AWS_REGION, which does not resolve a region
